Apparition

ap-uh-RISH-un · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Apparition is a ghost or ghost-like figure; a supernatural or startling sudden appearance.

The night watchman swore he saw an apparition drifting through the abandoned hallway just before the lights flickered out.

Worked Example

Visitors to the old lighthouse often report an apparition of a woman in a long coat, standing at the top of the stairs and staring out to sea.

An apparition is specifically a ghostly or supernatural-seeming figure -- not just any surprising sight.

How Strong Is It? — shadow → apparition → haunting

shadow vs. apparition

shadow vs. apparition: A shadow is a faint, hard-to-see shape, not necessarily supernatural.

haunting vs. apparition

haunting vs. apparition: A haunting is a persistent, unsettling supernatural presence, even more intense than a single apparition.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — appar-

root — appar-: to appear, come into view (Latin apparere)

suffix — -ition

suffix — -ition: the act, process, or result of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Apparition comes from Latin apparere ('to appear') -- the same root as apparent. It literally means 'an appearing,' which came to describe a ghost: something that suddenly, eerily appears.

Use the root in a new word: apparent

Use the root in a new word: apparent: It was apparent to everyone in the room that she was nervous.
